name: Oded
title: The Prophet Who Freed the Captives
summary: Oded was a prophet in Samaria during the time of the divided kingdom. He is best known for confronting the Israelite army as they returned with captives from Judah, demanding that the prisoners be released. His courageous intervention led to the Judean captives being treated with mercy and sent back to their homeland.

keyEvents.title: The War Between Israel and Judah
keyEvents.description: King Pekah of Israel defeated Judah in war during the reign of King Ahaz and took 200,000 captives back to Samaria.

keyEvents.title: Oded Confronts the Israelite Army
keyEvents.description: Prophet Oded went out to meet the Israelite army outside Samaria and declared that their victory was the Lord's judgment on Judah, but that they had gone too far by taking captives and incurred God's wrath.

keyEvents.title: Warning of the Lord's Wrath
keyEvents.description: Oded warned the Israelites that the Lord's burning anger rested upon them because they intended to make the Judeans into slaves, and he commanded them to send the captives back.

keyEvents.title: The Leaders of Ephraim Support the Prophet's Words
keyEvents.description: Four leaders among the heads of Ephraim supported Oded's message and opposed the army returning from war, insisting that the captives must be released.

keyEvents.title: The captives are treated with mercy
keyEvents.description: The named leaders took care of the captives, clothed the naked, gave them food and drink, anointed them, and led the weak on donkeys back to Jericho in Judah.

keyEvents.title: Ahaz's continued disobedience
keyEvents.description: Despite Oded's prophetic intervention and God's mercy, King Ahaz of Judah continued to act unfaithfully toward the Lord, leading to further suffering for the nation.
